verdict.rationale: Solid builds on JSX and TypeScript. Components are plain JavaScript functions, a div is a real DOM div, and the docs claim you don't have to learn a new rendering system; community users from React and Vue call it approachable and intuitive. However, hands-on reports describe Solid-specific concepts to learn: destructuring props can lose reactivity, props must be passed as functions, and the special props object adds friction. One critic also finds the JSX verbose compared to plain HTML. missing for 10: any evidence on using standard styling/CSS, and a way to avoid the reactivity-specific rules (e.g. a lint for lost reactivity) that add new concepts.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write components using standard markup, styling, and language syntax I already know, minimizing new concepts to learn

citations.quote: Solid is built on established tools like JSX and TypeScript and integrates with the Vite ecosystem.

In Solid, components are just functions - rendering is determined purely by how your state is used - so you're free to organize your code how you like and you don't have to learn a new rendering system.
your components are regular JavaScript functions that run once to set up your view
A `<div>` is a real div, so you can use your browser's devtools to inspect the rendering
